papers_read.title_as_printed: Brain Function Network: Higher Order vs. More Discrimination (Guo et al., Front. Neurosci. 2021)
Multiple Connection Pattern Combination From Single-Mode Data for Mild Cognitive Impairment Identification (Li et al., Front. Cell Dev. Biol. 2021)

what_each_reports.P-516: MCI vs HC from ADNI rs-fMRI (143 participants, 299 scans), linear SVM on t-test-selected edges, subject-level 5-fold CV. Accuracy of PCn networks falls as order n rises and approaches 50% when the iterated network converges; PC1 (ordinary Pearson) is best; all numeric values appear only in figures. Fusing PCn with PC1 raises sensitivity but not accuracy.
what_each_reports.P-523: MCI vs NC from ADNI rs-fMRI (63 MCI, 64 NC), nested LOOCV. Single first-order patterns: PC 77.95%, SR 81.10%, GCM 72.44%; the multi-kernel combination (MCPC) of PC, SR and GCM reaches 87.40% accuracy (sens 90.48%, spec 84.38%, AUC 0.922).

quantity_a: Accuracy of a deliberately degraded, iterated correlation-of-correlation (PCconv) network in MCI vs HC; the ~50% figure is the end point of an ablation, not the paper's best classifier.
quantity_b: Accuracy of a multi-kernel combination of three first-order connectivity estimators (Pearson, sparse partial correlation, Granger causality) in MCI vs NC.
incompatible_if_same: No. P-516's claim is that higher-order PCn networks discriminate worse than first-order PC1; P-523 uses only first-order estimators and reports nothing about higher-order networks, so neither result contradicts the other. Their first-order baselines (P-516 PC1, figure only; P-523 PC 77.95%) are not in conflict.

gates.task: match: both T1 MCI vs controls.
gates.validation_tier: match at internal CV (V3 in registry), but different schemes: subject-level 5-fold CV vs nested LOOCV.
gates.modality_family: match: resting-state fMRI; different feature constructions (higher-order PCn vs combined first-order patterns).

endpoint_and_metric: compatible metric (accuracy) but the P-516 value is an ablation asymptote, not a performance claim for a comparable model.
performance_validity: not a comparison of best performances; flag not triggered (P-523 87.4% is below the ceiling test; P-516's value is ~50%).
independence: Both draw on ADNI rs-fMRI; participant overlap is possible but not stated (shared cohort recorded as non-independence).
grounds: The record's claim for P-516 misreads its paper: ~50% is where accuracy lands when the PCn network is iterated to convergence, the degradation end point P-516 demonstrates, not its result for a usable network.
P-516 concludes that higher order does not help discrimination; P-523's MCPC contains no higher-order network, so P-523's 87.40% cannot refute or be refuted by P-516.
The two papers say compatible things: first-order connectivity carries the discriminative information, and combining views can add some (P-516 sensitivity, P-523 accuracy).

record_defects: claim_a and P-516's registry Best_Metric 'Acc ~50% at convergence' report an ablation end point as the paper's result; P-516 reports its accuracies only in figures and its best network is PC1.
validation_comparable 'Yes' glosses a difference in schemes (subject-level 5-fold CV on 143 participants with repeated scans vs nested LOOCV on 127).
The status 'partially_resolved_candidate' conflicts with the record's own G4 note, which found a non-contradiction; P-822's 'AUC 0.71' in the bridging list does not bear on the pair.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A higher-order-network result in P-523, or a P-516 claim that combined first-order patterns cannot exceed PC1; neither paper contains one.
